ci.latest_flow.source: latest: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs per head SHA, the latest pull request head that went all green; each stage's latest run of the last 20 per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them), with its pass rate over those 20; review and deploy stages from the latest of the last 20 merged pull requests; stages from .claude/settings.json, the git hooks in params.hooks_dir, .github/workflows and params.stages

ci.latest_full_run_minutes.source: latest: GraphQL check runs and steps of the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them), each workflow's latest run that did real work

ci.main_red_minutes.source: state: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, each workflow's runs on a push to the default branch: when its latest decided run failed, red from the end of the first failure after its latest success

ci.latest_pr_dollars.source: latest: the latest of the last 20 merged pull requests (when it opened before the runs read cover every workflow, or only runs its merge started are still going, the newest before it that can be priced, each one passed over named in the note; could_not_check when none can, or a branch run of it is still going); its runs (its branch's pull_request runs and its merge commit's push runs, gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs), each priced from its own jobs (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most: each job's billed minutes, rounded up, times its runs-on label's list rate: ubuntu-slim $0.002, Linux 2-core x64 $0.006, Linux 2-core arm64 $0.005, Windows $0.010, macOS 3 or 4-core $0.062 a minute, GitHub docs, Actions runner pricing, read 2026-11-03)

issues.latest_fix_ci_minutes.source: latest: the latest merged pull request that closed an issue (GraphQL closingIssuesReferences; when it opened before the runs read cover every workflow, or only runs its merge started are still going, the newest such one before it that can be priced, each one passed over named in the note; could_not_check when none can, or a branch run of it is still going); its runs (gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs), each job's billed minutes from its own jobs (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most, rounded up to the minute), summed and divided by the issues it closed

security.latest_scan_minutes.source: latest: gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs (each job's billed minutes, rounded up) for each workflow whose name matches params.security_workflows: the repo's own, its latest run that did real work of the newest 10 of its last 20 runs (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them); GitHub's dynamic ones such as CodeQL default setup, their latest passed run; summed. GitHub's dynamic CodeQL - Code Quality run is left out: code.quality_scan_minutes reads it

code.quality_scan_minutes.source: latest: gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs (each job's billed minutes, rounded up) for GitHub's dynamic workflow named CodeQL - Code Quality, its latest passed run, read with the security scans, so no extra request

ci.light_run_share.source: GraphQL check runs and steps (step conclusions) of the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median and a p90, few enough that new runs replace them); weighted by each workflow and event's runs since the start of the shortest full list of 100

ci.latest_main_push_minutes.source: latest: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, the push runs of the latest commit on the default branch whose runs all ended (the run collecting and any push with a run still going passed over, up to 5, each named in the note); their REST jobs (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs, one call per run at most): each job's billed minutes, rounded up, summed

ci.skip_unchanged_share.source: state: .github/workflows, each pull_request and push to main trigger: a paths or paths-ignore filter, a job whose if reads a needs.*.outputs value (a changes job), or a job calling ci-standard.yml with paths

ci.flaky_reruns.source: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median and a p90, few enough that new runs replace them), and runs/{id}/attempts/1 for every rerun that passed; a later pass counts on a push, and on a pull request only as a rerun

ci.cache_hit_rate.source: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs (setup-node's npm cache line, newest 12 jobs of the last 20 runs per workflow)

ci.queue_seconds_p90.source: last 10 completed runs per workflow, the queue sample the CI tab already reads (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs): each job's started_at less created_at

ci.failed_run_share.source: gh api actions/workflows/{id}/runs, the last 20 runs per workflow (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new runs replace them): runs that ended failure, timed_out or startup_failure, over those that passed or failed, on any event

insights.failed_minutes_share.source: GraphQL check runs of the last 20 runs per workflow: each job's minutes rounded up as GitHub bills them, summed for runs that ended cancelled, timed_out or startup_failure, or failed outside a pull request or merge queue, over all

ci.runner_cents_per_minute.source: last 10 completed runs per workflow, the queue sample the Actions tab already reads (gh api actions/runs/{id}/jobs): each job's billed minutes, rounded up, times its runs-on label's list rate (RUNNER_RATES), over the minutes; could_not_check when a job ran on a runner with no list price

ci.api_headroom.source: latest: gh api rate_limit (counts against no limit), each bucket's remaining over its limit, read with the token the run holds: latest.json the CI run's, local.json the account's login

ci.pr_run_requests.source: latest: gh api actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs (green pull_request runs from this repo), of the newest 3 the first whose jobs printed a notice, its jobs and their check-run annotations: each job's GitHub requests notice from quality/gh-replay.mjs, live REST plus GraphQL, summed

code.loc_change_pct.source: last N merged PRs: code lines now against main just before its last params.merged_prs merged PRs, counted from git's tree with the same rules (git log --first-parent of origin/<branch>, then <branch>, then HEAD, where the branch is ci.json's params.default_branch, else params.main_branch; with neither, HEAD; ls-tree, cat-file); detail is lines added less removed per area. N is params.merged_prs, 20 by default: a repo sets it so N merged PRs turn over within hours at its own merge rate

code.long_files.source: state: code lines per .ts, .mjs, .astro, .css, .py and .sh file in params.areas; a comment or a Python docstring is not a code line (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

code.long_functions.source: state: TypeScript compiler API, and Python's ast through one python3 -I call, code lines per function in params.areas (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

code.complex_functions.source: state: TypeScript compiler API over .ts, .mjs and .astro script blocks, and Python's ast over .py files through one python3 -I call, in params.areas (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

code.duplicated_pct.source: state: runs of 5+ code lines and 50+ tokens (jscpd's defaults) seen earlier in params.areas, line-based (quality/collectors/code/shape.mjs)

code.dead_files.source: state: knip --reporter json, files inside params.areas

code.dead_exports.source: state: knip --reporter json: unused exports, types, enum, namespace and class members inside params.areas

code.dead_dependencies.source: state: knip --reporter json: dependencies, devDependencies and optional peers in every package.json

code.dead_functions.source: state: each .py file's top-level functions in params.areas (Python's ast through one python3 -I call) whose name no .py file there, tests and fixtures included, reads, imports, reaches as an attribute or holds as a string; a method is not judged (quality/collectors/code/code-python.mjs)

code.drift_markers.source: state: TODO, FIXME and XXX inside comments in params.areas

code.commented_code.source: state: 3 or more comment lines in a row that parse as TypeScript statements, in params.areas

code.missing_refs.source: state: repo paths in comments and strings in params.areas that git log shows were committed and are now gone (needs full history: fetch-depth 0)

code.export_comments_pct.source: state: exported functions in params.areas with a comment ending on the line above (TypeScript compiler API), and each .py file's public top-level functions with a docstring or such a comment (Python's ast)

code.purpose_comments_pct.source: state: code files in params.areas whose first thing, after any shebang or .astro fence, is a comment of 3+ words besides tool directives (quality/collectors/code/complexity.mjs)

code.naming_pct.source: state: git ls-files in params.areas, each code file and each folder holding one against the first rule in params.naming whose path pattern matches it, a folder as its path ending in a slash (quality/collectors/code/shape.mjs); by default .astro components PascalCase, pages kebab-case or [param], .py and .sh snake_case, other code and folders kebab-case

code.mapped_areas_pct.source: state: git ls-files: each area in params.areas named as a folder, its path ending in a slash, in a table row or a mermaid block of a README.md above it or of a Markdown doc that README links in its own folder, or holding a README.md with a table or a diagram of its own (quality/collectors/code/code-structure.mjs)

code.import_cycles.source: state: relative imports and re-exports of each .ts, .mjs and .js file in params.areas (TypeScript compiler API) and sibling-module imports of each .py file; strongly connected groups of two or more files (quality/collectors/code/code-cycles.mjs)

code.test_coverage_pct.source: state: vitest v8 coverage, json-summary, or for a params.test_suites suite with runner node, the node --test --experimental-test-coverage lcov its CI job printed (code-lcov.mjs), read from that workflow's newest successful run on the default branch; in ci mode only: covered lines plus covered branches over all lines plus branches of each suite's cover folders, suites summed, never averaged; lines only, with the suite named, when a report has no branch data. node counts only the files a test loads

code.worker_wall_max_ms.source: last N requests: cf workers deployments list per Worker in params.workers (the first is the one serving traffic), then cf sql query on logs.workersLogs, the newest params.last_requests fetch invocations since that deploy; the largest wallTimeMs, worst Worker; local mode only. N is params.last_requests (100 by default): a repo sets it so that many requests turn over within hours at its own traffic

code.worker_cpu_max_ms.source: last N requests: cf workers deployments list per Worker in params.workers, then cf sql query on logs.workersLogs, the newest params.last_requests fetch invocations since that deploy; the largest cpuTimeMs, worst Worker; local mode only. N is params.last_requests (100 by default): a repo sets it so that many requests turn over within hours at its own traffic

code.worker_bundle_kb.source: state: wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir <tmp> in each folder of params.workers; gzip of the bundled modules; the largest Worker

code.client_js_kb.source: state: the built static site in params.client_dist.dir: each page's first-party scripts, modulepreloads and their imports, gzipped; heaviest page. A build older than the newest commit touching params.client_dist.source is not measured

code.build_seconds.source: latest: wall time of wrangler deploy --dry-run for each folder of params.workers, this run

code.check_seconds.source: latest: wall time of params.check's job in its workflow's newest successful run on the default branch; detail is that job in each of the newest successful runs

code.code_tokens.source: state: bytes of the code files in each area of params.areas, tests included, over params.bytes_per_token; the largest area. An area leaves out any folder that is an area of its own

code.largest_file_tokens.source: state: bytes of the largest code file in params.areas, tests included, over params.bytes_per_token; detail is the ten largest

code.worker_startup_ms.source: latest: per Worker in params.workers, cf workers get (its tag), cf builds list (the newest successful Workers Build) and cf builds logs get: the Worker Startup Time that wrangler deploy printed; the slowest Worker; local mode only

deploy.waiting_merges.source: npx wrangler deployments list --json and npx wrangler versions list --json (read-only, the 10 most recent of each) in .; git log --first-parent origin/main; merges on main touching any path that production does not hold now; detail is hours each has waited; the latest code deploy, 2026-11-28T03:14Z, holds 5960fbd (main when it was uploaded)

deploy.oldest_waiting_hours.source: npx wrangler deployments list --json and npx wrangler versions list --json (read-only, the 10 most recent of each) in .; git log --first-parent origin/main; hours since the oldest merge production does not hold was merged, 0 when none waits; the latest code deploy, 2026-11-28T03:14Z, holds 5960fbd (main when it was uploaded)

deploy.latest_lead_hours.source: npx wrangler deployments list --json and npx wrangler versions list --json (read-only, the 10 most recent of each) in .; git log --first-parent origin/main; the latest deploy that shipped a merge, 2026-11-28T03:13Z (5960fbd): hours from its earliest merge to the deploy

deploy.latest_failed.source: npx wrangler deployments list --json and npx wrangler versions list --json (read-only, the 10 most recent of each) in .; git log --first-parent origin/main; a deploy failed when the next one rolled it back or when it first shipped a PR that a bug issue names in a "Regressed-by: #N" line (gh issue list -R Colorado-Startups/space-peak --search "Regressed-by" in:body); restored at the rollback or at the first deploy after the issue closed; 1 when the latest code deploy failed or was itself a rollback

deploy.failure_rate_last10.source: npx wrangler deployments list --json and npx wrangler versions list --json (read-only, the 10 most recent of each) in .; git log --first-parent origin/main; a deploy failed when the next one rolled it back or when it first shipped a PR that a bug issue names in a "Regressed-by: #N" line (gh issue list -R Colorado-Startups/space-peak --search "Regressed-by" in:body); restored at the rollback or at the first deploy after the issue closed; the last 10 code deploys (secret-only deploys left out), N = 10 because Wrangler lists only the 10 most recent

deploy.latest_restore_hours.could_not_check: none of the last 10 deploys failed, so there is nothing to restore
deploy.latest_restore_hours.source: npx wrangler deployments list --json and npx wrangler versions list --json (read-only, the 10 most recent of each) in .; git log --first-parent origin/main; a deploy failed when the next one rolled it back or when it first shipped a PR that a bug issue names in a "Regressed-by: #N" line (gh issue list -R Colorado-Startups/space-peak --search "Regressed-by" in:body); restored at the rollback or at the first deploy after the issue closed

deploy.latest_build_minutes.source: latest: the workflow runs the push to main of the latest production deploy's commit started (gh api actions/runs?head_sha=&event=push, then runs/{id}/jobs), each job rounded up to the whole minute as GitHub bills it (docs.github.com/en/billing/managing-billing-for-github-actions/about-billing-for-github-actions); Workers Builds minutes are not read; the deploy of 2026-11-28T03:14Z (5960fbd)

design.raw_hex.source: state: regex scan of params.src_dirs (params.scan_extensions), comments stripped; params.raw_scan_exempt says which files or lines are left out, and why

design.raw_px.source: state: regex scan of params.src_dirs (params.scan_extensions), comments stripped; params.raw_scan_exempt says which files or lines are left out

design.font_sizes_off_scale.source: state: Playwright (Chrome) computed font-size of visible text on params.key_pages at params.widths, against the type scale in params.tokens (within 0.5 px)

design.text_colors_off_token.source: state: Playwright (Chrome) computed color of visible text on params.key_pages at params.widths, against the colors in params.tokens

design.contrast_violations.source: state: axe-core color-contrast (the version installed in the repo, else beside the collectors) injected by Playwright (Chrome), params.key_pages at params.widths

design.lcp_mobile.source: latest: PageSpeed Insights API v5, strategy=mobile, lab LCP, params.key_pages; a page PSI cannot answer, and every page of a built static site, is measured by our own Playwright lab run under Lighthouse's mobile settings and marked (lab)

design.cls_mobile.source: latest: PageSpeed Insights API v5, strategy=mobile, lab CLS, params.key_pages; a page PSI cannot answer, and every page of a built static site, is measured by our own Playwright lab run under Lighthouse's mobile settings and marked (lab)

design.total_bytes.source: state: Playwright (Chrome) network log, all responses at load, params.key_pages at params.widths

docs.dead_paths.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: each word of inline code and code blocks in the doc set that starts with a top-level repo entry and exists neither from the repo root nor from the doc's folder; git-ignored paths and records (docs with an empty area in params.areas) skipped. A heuristic

docs.dead_scripts.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: npm run, npm test and npm start in inline code and code blocks of the doc set, against the scripts of the root package.json and its workspaces; with -w, against that workspace alone. Records (docs with an empty area in params.areas) are skipped

docs.broken_links.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: relative markdown links and #anchors in the doc set, resolved against the repo and GitHub heading slugs

docs.lint_warn.source: state: params.lint over the doc set: the summary line 'N file(s) checked, X FAIL, Y WARN'. Docs outside the lint's scope are skipped by the lint. A repo with no params.lint names no lint, and this metric is not measured

docs.markup_faults.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: in each doc of the doc set, outside code, a heading more than one level below the one before it, an H1 after the first, a heading whose text repeats at its level anywhere in the doc, and an image with no alt text or alt text over params.alt_max_chars

docs.stale_markers.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: each of params.markers outside code and comments in the doc set, counted per doc

docs.stale_dates.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: each params.as_of phrase and its date outside code in the doc set, against the last commit to the doc's area in params.areas; detail is days older

docs.oldest_lag_days.source: state: git log -1 --format=%ct for each doc and for its area in params.areas; the largest gap of any doc now, which the detail names

docs.unmapped.source: state: each doc in params.doc_set against params.areas, the first entry whose doc glob matches, and each area path it names through git ls-files. A path that matches no tracked file is dead, and so is an area whose paths together match only the doc; an area of [] is a record, mapped on purpose; the detail names each doc and path

docs.folder_coverage.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: top-level folders, less dot folders and git-ignored ones, with a README or a row under params.folder_map.heading in params.folder_map.doc

docs.runbooks_verified.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: "last verified <date>" (params.verified) outside code in each of params.runbooks, less params.doc_set_left_out; detail is the newest date

docs.community_files.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: each entry of params.community_files (README, license, contributing guide, code of conduct, support file, pull request template) with a file at any of its globs

docs.over_read_goal.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: docs of params.doc_set with more words than params.minutes_goal times params.words_per_minute, counted by top-level folder

docs.interactive_share.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: docs of the doc set outside params.agent_docs with a mermaid diagram, a mermaid chart (params.mermaid_charts) or a <details> block, outside code; detail counts each element type

docs.text_only.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: docs of the doc set whose table (two or more columns; a one-column table is a list), code, diagram and image lines are under params.text_only_below percent of their non-blank lines, counted by top-level folder

docs.tokens_past_read_goal.source: state: quality/collectors/docs/docs.mjs: bytes / 4 of each doc of params.doc_set (the estimate the Instructions tab uses), the share of its words past params.minutes_goal times params.words_per_minute, summed; detail is the heaviest docs

issues.open_bugs.source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, open issues of the Bug type (params.bug_type; on a user's repo, which has no types, the label params.bug_label), by area label (params.area_labels)

issues.parked_open.source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, open issues older than params.park_hours whose issueType is not in params.issue_types; not measured for a user's repo, which has no issue types

issues.area_labeled.source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, labels named in params.area_labels

issues.stray_labels.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/labels (archived_at) and gh api graphql: repository.labels (issues and pullRequests totalCount); a label not archived that nothing carries and that is neither params.bug_label nor in params.area_labels

issues.intake_ready.source: state: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE: each YAML issue form parsed for the keys GitHub requires (name, description, body) and its type, and config.yml for blank_issues_enabled; a form that does not parse is a miss, as GitHub rejects it; the type check is against params.issue_types and is left out when that is empty

issues.closed_by_pr.source: gh api graphql: repository.issues, the last 20 issues of the Bug type (params.bug_type; on a user's repo, the label params.bug_label) closed as completed (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new closes replace them), ClosedEvent closer (a merged PR, or a commit from one); left out before the 20 are taken: not-planned and duplicate closes, and a record, closed by hand within params.record_minutes of opening

issues.reopened.source: gh api graphql: repository.issues, the last 20 issues closed as completed (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new closes replace them), REOPENED_EVENT count; not-planned and duplicate closes, and a record closed by hand within params.record_minutes of opening, left out

issues.latest_close_hours.source: latest: gh api graphql: repository.issues, the latest issue closed as completed (a point in time, never a median over a window): closedAt minus createdAt; a not-planned or duplicate close, or a record closed by hand within params.record_minutes of opening, is left out

issues.oldest_open_days.source: state: gh api graphql: repository.issues, open issues, age at read time

issues.latest_card_words.source: latest: gh api graphql: of the 20 newest issues (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new issues replace them), the latest with a body; words left after removing tables, fenced code and diagrams, inline code, link targets, HTML comments and params.pr_body_ignore (proseWords in github.mjs)

issues.card_visual_share.source: gh api graphql: the body of each of the 20 newest issues (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new issues replace them); a table, a Mermaid, GeoJSON, TopoJSON or STL block, or an image outside code (hasVisual in github.mjs)

pull_requests.green_at_head.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them), head commit statusCheckRollup: state SUCCESS, or each check's latest run passed, since the rollup also counts an earlier run of a check that ran again on the same commit

pull_requests.reviewed.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); reviewed when a person submitted a review whose commit.oid is the merged headRefOid, or a member posted a comment whose first line is Review: MERGE at that SHA, no later than mergedAt (bot reviews left out)

pull_requests.fixed_after_review.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them) with a person's review, or a member's Review: MERGE|BLOCK at <sha> comment, before the merge; fixed when that first one read a commit other than the merged head, as a BLOCK at an earlier head does

pull_requests.reverted.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); a PR titled Revert "<title>" undoes the merged PR with that title, and every such revert among the 20 counts

pull_requests.commits_via_pr.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 commits on the default branch (N = 20, as for merged PRs: each merge adds at least one commit), associatedPullRequests merged

pull_requests.merged_off_default.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them), baseRefName other than its base repository's defaultBranchRef.name, read in the same query; each with its reviewed lines

pull_requests.latest_body_words.source: latest: gh api graphql: of the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: few enough that new merges replace them), the latest with a description; words left after removing tables, fenced code and diagrams, inline code, link targets, HTML comments and params.pr_body_ignore (proseWords in github.mjs)

pull_requests.body_table_share.source: gh api graphql: the body of each of the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); a markdown table row followed by its separator row, outside fenced blocks (hasTable in github.mjs)

pull_requests.linked_issue_share.source: gh api graphql: the body of each of the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them); a closing keyword (close, fix or resolve) or Part of before an issue reference, outside fenced blocks (linksIssue in github.mjs)

pull_requests.latest_lines.source: latest: gh api graphql: the latest merged pullRequest, additions plus deletions, less the lines of lockfiles, generated code, data snapshots and params.not_reviewed (NOT_REVIEWED in github.mjs), and the lines of files removed whole (changeType DELETED), and two for each line its merge commit moves, one when it left with a removed file (git diff, readLines in github-reviews.mjs)

pull_requests.over_400_lines.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, a template choice: enough for a median, few enough that new merges replace them), additions plus deletions, less lockfile, generated and snapshot lines, files removed whole (changeType DELETED) and the lines each merge commit moves (git diff, readLines in github-reviews.mjs)

pull_requests.latest_merge_hours.source: latest: gh api graphql: the latest merged pullRequest (a point in time, never a median over a window): mergedAt minus createdAt; its stages from head check times and reviews at head

pull_requests.green_to_merge_minutes.source: gh api graphql: the last 10 merged pullRequests (N = 10, a template choice), median of mergedAt minus the last check's completion on the merged head, for each PR whose head rollup is SUCCESS

pull_requests.open_now.source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests, by age at read time

pull_requests.green_waiting_minutes.source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests that are not drafts, not Dependabot's, green at head (statusCheckRollup SUCCESS) and not blocked there (a Review: BLOCK verdict, or reviewDecision CHANGES_REQUESTED); the longest time since the head's last check completed, at read time, the five longest as rows

pull_requests.conflicting.source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests, mergeable is CONFLICTING

pull_requests.oldest_open_days.source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests, age at read time

pull_requests.dependabot_open.source: state: gh api graphql: open pullRequests authored by dependabot, by ecosystem label

actions.pinned_share.source: state: .github/workflows/*.yml: each job's and step's uses:, read from the parsed YAML, ending in a 40-character SHA, or a step's reference that .github/workflows/actions.lock records for its workflow; local ./ and $/ actions left out

actions.permissions_share.source: state: .github/workflows/*.yml: a top-level permissions: block, or one on every job

actions.locked_share.source: state: each .github/workflows/*.yml with an outside action in a step, against the workflows listed in .github/workflows/actions.lock; a workflow with only a job-level call or local actions is left out, since a lockfile does not cover them

security.code_scanning_on.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-scanning/default-setup (state configured) or code-scanning/analyses; off is a miss even when the plan charges for it

security.secret_scanning_on.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}: security_and_analysis.secret_scanning and secret_scanning_push_protection both enabled; off is a miss even when the plan charges for it

security.code_quality_on.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-quality/setup (state configured); off is a miss even when the plan charges for it

security.dependabot_open.source: state: gh api dependabot/alerts: open alerts that are vulnerabilities (malware left out), by security_advisory.severity

security.malware_open.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/dependabot/alerts --paginate: open alerts whose security_advisory.classification is malware

security.code_scanning_open.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-scanning/alerts --paginate: open alerts by severity; could_not_check while code scanning is off

security.secret_scanning_open.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/secret-scanning/alerts --paginate: open alerts by secret type; could_not_check while secret scanning is off

security.code_quality_open.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/code-quality/findings?state=open --paginate, by severity; could_not_check while code quality is off

security.headers.source: state: HEAD params.site_url: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy

security.token_default_read.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow: default_workflow_permissions is read

security.actions_policy_share.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/permissions: allowed_actions is not all, and sha_pinning_required is true

security.prt_head_checkouts.source: state: .github/workflows/*.yml: jobs of a pull_request_target or workflow_run workflow that check out the pull request's code (actions/checkout of its head, gh pr checkout, or git fetch or checkout of refs/pull/*)

security.dependabot_cooldown.source: state: .github/dependabot.yml: each updates entry's shortest cooldown days against params.cooldown_days

security.lockfile_registry_share.source: state: package-lock.json at the root: each package's resolved URL against params.registries, parsed: https, the registry's host, under its path

security.young_lockfile_packages.source: state: package-lock.json against itself params.cooldown_days ago (git); each entry added since on an allowed registry (parsed: https, its host, under its path): a HEAD of its download for Last-Modified, then the registry's full document only where that is recent; no redirects, at most params.max_registry_reads requests; could_not_check on a shallow clone, an unreachable registry or a missing publish time

security.threat_model_current.source: state: git log at the root: the latest commit to params.threat_model (a path, or a list of paths that must all exist) against the latest to params.threat_model_covers, less params.threat_model_grace_days; could_not_check on a shallow clone or with no covered paths

security.claude_review_share.source: gh api graphql: the last 20 merged pullRequests (N = 20, as for the Pull requests tab): a head check run from an app in params.review_apps, or a review or comment by a Bot whose login is in params.review_authors, named like params.security_review; only PRs that change a file params.review_paths names, when it names any

security.latest_fix_days.source: latest: gh api dependabot/alerts, and code-scanning/alerts and secret-scanning/alerts while those features are on: the latest fixed alert, fixed_at or resolved_at (revoked) minus created_at

security.oldest_open_alert_days.source: state: gh api dependabot/alerts, and code-scanning/alerts, secret-scanning/alerts and code-quality/findings while those features are on: the oldest open one's age at read time

security.features_dollars_per_month.source: state: gh api orgs/{owner}/settings/billing/advanced-security, active committers billed for Code Security and Secret Protection, times their list prices ($30 and $19 a month, github.com/security/plans, read 2026-11-03); Code Quality's per-seat licence is not in this read

settings.main_protected.source: state: gh api branches/{branch}/protection and rules/branches/{branch}, {branch} the default branch: a pull request required, force pushes blocked, deletion blocked

settings.required_checks.source: state: gh api branches/{branch}/protection required_status_checks and rules/branches/{branch} required_status_checks, {branch} the default branch

settings.pages_private.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/pages: public is false; not measured for a public repo, a user's repo, or an organization whose plan is not Enterprise (gh api repos/{repo}, orgs/{owner})

settings.dependabot_grouping.source: state: .github/dependabot.yml: updates entries with a groups: block

insights.community_health_pct.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/community/profile, GitHub's health percentage and the files it found

insights.leftover_branches.source: state: GraphQL refs under refs/heads (the first 1000) with their pull requests: a branch whose pull request closed or merged, or one older than params.branch_grace_hours (24) with none; the default branch, open pull requests and params.keep_branches do not count

insights.oldest_leftover_hours.source: state: GraphQL refs under refs/heads (the first 1000) with their pull requests: a branch whose pull request closed or merged, or one older than params.branch_grace_hours (24) with none; the default branch, open pull requests and params.keep_branches do not count; each timed from its pull request's close, or from its last commit

insights.idle_access.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/collaborators (people who can push, the first 100) and each one's latest default-branch commit: those with none in params.idle_days days (90, the benchmark's line); org owners left out, since GitHub recommends at least two and no repo review can remove one

settings.protections_missing.source: state: gh api rulesets and each active one (bypass_actors, tag rules deletion and update, push rule file_path_restriction against params.blocked_paths), branches/{branch}/protection (enforce_admins), tags (the first listed), environments (deployment_branch_policy); a row with nothing to guard is left out

settings.general_drift.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}, each field named in params.expected against its value there

settings.outside_access.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/collaborators?affiliation=outside and repos/{repo}/invitations, counted

settings.unused_secrets.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/secrets and each environment's secrets (names only), against secrets.NAME in .github/workflows/*.yml of the checkout

settings.person_waits.source: state: pull_request rules of the active rulesets on the default branch and of its classic protection (approvals, code owner review, last-push approval, required reviewers), and each environment's protection_rules (required_reviewers, wait_timer)

settings.metered_on.source: state: gh api repos/{repo}/actions/cache/storage-limit (max_cache_size_gb against params.included_cache_gb) and the active rulesets' copilot_code_review rules; not measured for a public repo

settings.open_repo_missing.source: state: gh api repos/{repo} (has_discussions, security_and_analysis.secret_scanning_push_protection), repos/{repo}/actions/permissions/fork-pr-contributor-approval (approval_policy) and repos/{repo}/private-vulnerability-reporting (enabled); not measured for a private repo

settings.admin_read_age_hours.source: state: generated_at of local.json in the repo's data folder, the last collect.mjs --local run, against the time of this CI run

tests.axe_routes.source: state: page files in params.pages_dir and the site paths named by the e2e suite's specs that run AxeBuilder

tests.site_tests_p50.source: last N passing jobs: gh api runs of the suite workflow in params.workflows (newest 100 runs a workflow), with GraphQL check runs: the last 20 passing test jobs. N is 20 (ci.mjs's LAST_RUNS): enough to turn over within hours where the test workflows run many times a day

tests.e2e_shard_p50.source: last N passing jobs: gh api runs of the e2e workflow in params.workflows (newest 100 runs a workflow), with GraphQL check runs: the last 20 passing jobs of each shard. N is 20 (ci.mjs's LAST_RUNS): enough to turn over within hours where the test workflows run many times a day

tests.ci_minutes_latest_main.source: latest: the latest completed run of each workflow in params.workflows whose test jobs ran, on main where the workflow runs there, else its latest pull request run (newest 100 runs a workflow); GitHub bills each job by the whole minute

tools.deps_latest_share.source: state: package.json (root and workspaces) with its lockfile (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, pnpm-lock.yaml or yarn.lock) and npm view <name> time --json

tools.adopters_latest_share.source: state: each params.adopters repo's .github/workflows uses: pins (gh api contents), this repo's version tags (gh api tags) and the committer date of each tag younger than that, highest version first, up to the first old enough (gh api git/commits). tools.oldest_update_wait_days.source: state: npm view <name> time --json against the lockfile

tools.oldest_dependency_pr_days.source: state: gh pr list --label params.dependency_label --state open

tools.npm_ci_seconds.source: latest: gh api actions/runs (or params.install_workflow's runs) and runs/{id}/jobs, the newest successful push run with an npm ci, pnpm install or yarn install step

usability.long_sentences.source: state: main element's prose, params.key_pages at the widest of params.widths, via Playwright (Chrome)

usability.unlabeled_fields.source: state: Playwright (Chrome) on params.form_pages, loaded and never submitted

usability.broken_links.source: state: GET crawl of the site from /, same origin, at most params.crawl_max fetches, params.crawl_skip never fetched

usability.keyboard_task_share.source: state: Playwright (Chrome) at 1280 px follows each task in params.tasks along its shortest route from / in the crawl, from a fresh load: on each page, Tab until the link that leads on has focus, then Enter, which must land on the next page. usability.words_before_action.source: state: visible words in main before its first link, button or field, params.key_pages at the widest of params.widths, via Playwright (Chrome)

usability.tbt_mobile.source: latest: PageSpeed Insights API v5, strategy=mobile, lab TBT, params.key_pages; a page PSI cannot answer, and every page of a built static site, is measured by our own Playwright lab run under Lighthouse's mobile settings and marked (lab)

usability.form_page_kib.source: state: Playwright (Chrome) network log, all responses at load, each of params.form_pages at 1280 px in a fresh context; value is the heaviest form page
